segments.en: It is still dark at Sossusvlei, and climbers are racing up a giant red dune to watch the first light spill across the Namib, one of the oldest deserts on Earth.
Nearby lies Deadvlei, a white clay pan dotted with dark, dead camel thorn trees that have stood there for hundreds of years, framed by orange dunes and a deep blue sky.
Along the Atlantic, the Skeleton Coast is wrapped in cool fog, and old shipwrecks rest on the sand. Inland, elephants and lions have learned to survive in the dry riverbeds.

In the north, Etosha National Park surrounds a vast salt pan that shimmers white. In the dry season, elephants, giraffes, zebras and rhinos gather at the waterholes, and floodlights let you watch them after dark.
Namibia is home to many peoples and many languages, from Oshiwambo and Otjiherero to Khoekhoegowab, with its clicking sounds, and Afrikaans and German, while English is the official language.
Herero women wear long, full dresses and a wide hat shaped like the horns of cattle, a proud symbol of their heritage and their herds.
In the northwest, Himba women coat their skin and braided hair with otjize, a mix of red ochre and butterfat that protects against the sun and is considered very beautiful.
At Twyfelfontein, ancient hunter-gatherers carved thousands of images of giraffes, rhinos and lions into the sandstone, and many of them are thousands of years old.
The capital, Windhoek, sits in the central highlands. Its sandstone Christ Church and older buildings recall the colonial era, while its busy markets are full of today's Namibian life.
Namibians love a braai, a barbecue under the stars with family and friends. In Windhoek's markets, try kapana, strips of beef grilled over the fire and dipped in spicy salt.
On the coast, Swakopmund is the place for sandboarding down dunes, and nearby Walvis Bay turns pink with flocks of flamingos.
Namibia was among the first countries to write protection of the environment into its constitution, and many rural communities help look after the wildlife on their land.
At night, far from any city, the sky is so dark and clear that the Milky Way seems close enough to touch.
Thank you for travelling with me. Head east across the Kalahari, and Botswana is waiting.
